attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a Kea DHCPv4 server on the private network (eth1/enp8s0, 10.50.50.0/24) shared with node2 and node3, and configured node2/node3 to obtain their address on that network via DHCP (systemd-networkd) instead of static assignment. Implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4, the pre-provisioned Ansible control node. Bootstrapped SSH access from node4 to node1 (vyos user, via VyOS's own config-managed public-keys so it survives reboots) and to node2/node3 (root; had to generate missing SSH host keys and enable the disabled sshd service). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, with boot-id-based proof of restart and post-restart verification that DHCP server config and client leases fully recovered. A final full playbook re-run after all restarts confirmed idempotency and correctness of the end state.
